entry.title: When they want you close
entry.summary: Davies makes room for toddlers who want company. Shared play or a small part of daily work can offer connection while you notice what help they need.
entry.cue: Your child wants to stay beside you, follows you, or asks you to do something together.
detail: Changes, temperament, divided attention, or difficulty managing an activity are among the possibilities Davies considers. None explains every child or every day.
She begins with playing together and gradually watching more while the child leads. She also includes the child in ordinary work, such as handling socks while the adult does laundry.
Toddlers still need supervision and are not expected to play alone for hours. In new places, she suggests helping them get oriented and saying where you are going instead of sneaking away.

references.locator: Possible context, normal supervision, shared play/work, understanding and announced departures
